# kenji: deliberate falsehoods and their ground truth

## K-L-01: he states a conclusion his own record does not support

**The lie.** His journal claim on the last day: *"The maintenance block held
me flat."*

**The ground truth**, and it is subtler than a wrong number. His own two
readings of that block disagree about the impression it gives:

- its least-squares slope is **+0.014 kg/week**, which is flat;
- its endpoints differ by **+0.65 kg**, which is **1.7 times** the SD of a
  difference between two readings at this scatter, and so is ordinary noise
  reading as a gain.

**Neither is wrong.** What is wrong is stating a conclusion from one of them,
and every Sunday note through that block says in terms that he cannot yet
separate the slope from zero. He asserted on the last day exactly the thing he
had spent thirteen weeks writing down that he could not establish.

**Why this lie and not a wrong number.** He is a metrologist. Giving him a
mistyped weight would test transcription, which four other personas already
carry. The error available to him and to nobody else here is the one he is
professionally trained against: reading a result off an instrument he had
himself argued was not up to the question. A corpus of people who make
arithmetic mistakes cannot exercise that.

**What the engine should do.** Observe the contradiction and not resolve it.
Two statements disagreeing is an observation. And its refusal to score a
weekly rate over that block is the CORRECT answer rather than a shortcoming -
he is the one person in this corpus who would say so himself.
